can_do_statement: Can use 'either' and 'neither' + 'of' with plural noun phrases or pronouns.► pronouns

ontology.mental_model: Specification of alternative or negative inclusion from a specific plural set.
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Using 'either of' or 'neither of' before a group.

positives: Either of the measures is recommended.
Neither of us could foresee the problem.

can_do_statement: Can use determiners in hyperbole, often in informal contexts ('millions of', 'loads of', 'tons of').

ontology.mental_model: Exaggeration of quantity for rhetorical effect.
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Using hyperbole like 'millions of' or 'tons of'.

positives: I managed to fit in millions of cookbooks.
I received tons of plastic ducks.
negatives: I have a million things to do.
She has a heavy load to carry.

can_do_statement: Can use 'either' and 'neither' with singular nouns.

ontology.pedagogical_hook: Using 'either' or 'neither' directly before a singular noun.

positives: Neither party could foresee the rise.
Either way is possible.
negatives: I like neither of the parties.
We didn't go that way either.

can_do_statement: Can use modifier + 'little' + uncountable nouns and modifier + 'few' + countable nouns, to indicate a lack of something or not as much as expected of something.► adverbs

ontology.mental_model: Emphasizing a scarcity or lack of quantity using modifiers.

positives: I spend very little time outside.
There are so few animals living there.
negatives: I have a little time left.

can_do_statement: Can modify determiners with adverbs. ► adverbs

positives: Because almost all of the programmes are stupid.
We've spent nearly every day together.
negatives: I have almost finished my homework.

guideword: FORM/USE: 'MANY A' WITH SINGULAR NOUNS, FOR FOCUS
can_do_statement: Can use 'many a' or 'many an' + singular noun for emphasis and focus.

ontology.mental_model: Literary or emphatic expression of multitude using singular forms.
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Using 'many a time' or 'many an issue'.

positives: We have climbed many a mountain.
It has raised many an issue.

guideword: FORM/USE: 'AS YOU KNOW', ORGANISING, MARKING SHARED KNOWLEDGE
can_do_statement: Can use 'as you know' as a discourse marker of shared knowledge.

ontology.mental_model: Signalling that the following information is already part of the listener's knowledge.
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Using 'as you know' to build rapport.

positives: As you know, I live in England.
Because, as you know, I am leaving tomorrow.
negatives: I know you as a good person.
As you can see, it is raining.

can_do_statement: Can use a range of words and phrases as discourse markers to add information.

ontology.mental_model: Structuring discourse by explicitly adding to previous points.

positives: Moreover the health of our staff is essential.
Furthermore, I think that you should exercise.
negatives: We will go further into the forest.

guideword: FORM/USE: ORGANISING, MARKING NEW KNOWLEDGE, INFORMAL
can_do_statement: Can use 'you see', 'the thing is' as discourse markers to mark new knowledge, usually in informal contexts.

ontology.mental_model: Introducing explanatory or new information conversationally.
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Using 'you see' or 'the thing is' to explain.

positives: You see, in the park, you can enjoy fresh air.
The thing is, I'd go to the countryside.

can_do_statement: Can use 'so' as a discourse marker to summarise, usually in informal contexts.

ontology.mental_model: Summarising or deducing consequences in conversational contexts.
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Using 'so' at the start of a clause to summarise.

positives: So, what do you think?
So I'll be at your house at 15.30.

can_do_statement: Can use sequencing adverbs as discourse markers to organise text.

ontology.mental_model: Structuring discourse logically using ordinal adverbs.

positives: Firstly, we need a good expert.
Secondly, good materials are needed.
negatives: He came first in the race.

can_do_statement: Can use a range of phrases as discourse markers to introduce contrasting statements.

ontology.pedagogical_hook: Using 'on the other hand' or 'on the contrary'.

positives: On the other hand I think you can learn better.
My new teacher, on the contrary, understands us.

can_do_statement: Can use a range of phrases as discourse markers to introduce a comparison.

ontology.mental_model: Drawing parallels between two states or events.

positives: Likewise, in Nepal New Year is celebrated on 1st of Baishak.
Similarly, the population of children are likely to drop.
negatives: He is very similar to me.

can_do_statement: Can use a range of phrases as discourse markers to summarise.

positives: Thus, I would be very grateful.
Consequently, visiting zoos can help people.
negatives: So I went to the store.

can_do_statement: Can use adverbs as discourse markers to indicate an attitude or viewpoint.

ontology.mental_model: Expressing speaker attitude or evaluation of a proposition.

positives: Unfortunately, they filmed only the building.
Actually, I do not have much time.
